correctness.rationale: With s_j=(-1)^floor(log2(j+1)) and F(0)=0 of slopes s_j, F is 1-Lipschitz, |F(t)|<=t. Thus beta(0)=1, n^-1<=beta(n)=2^[F(log2 n)]<=n, beta(n)^(1/n)->1, and n/(n+1)<=beta(n+1)/beta(n)<=(n+1)/n. Polynomial coefficient weights make H2(beta) analytic; C_z2 maps orthonormal e_n to d_n e_(2n) with d_n=beta(2n)/beta(n) in [1/2,2]; d_1=2 gives ||C_z2||=2. The span of e_(2^j), j>=0, is reducing for T and T*, supporting a unilateral positive shift with w_j=2^s_j; no off-orbit monomial maps onto it. For any positive shift, polar decomposition yields Delta weights sqrt(w_j w_(j+1)), and induction gives first coefficient b_N=2^[2^-N sum_{j=0}^N binom(N,j)s_j]. At N=3*2^ell, the Bin(N,1/2) mean is 3*2^(ell-1); the event |B-N/2|<2^(ell-2) lies wholly in j in [2^ell-1,2^(ell+1)-2], where s_j=(-1)^ell. Hoeffding bounds the complement by 2 exp(-2^ell/24), hence |E s_B-(-1)^ell|<=4exp(-2^ell/24), so b_N tends to 2 on even ell and 1/2 on odd ell. A fixed WOT coefficient diverges, disproving SOT convergence without finite-to-infinite extrapolation. Independent exact-rational binomial computations for ell=4..10 corroborated the formula and estimate; the infinite conclusion uses the analytic proof.

value.rationale: This explicit counterexample settles the published universal composition-operator Aluthge convergence question (Lahiri–Ojha–Birbonshi 2026, Q5.2) negatively, while preserving important analytic structure: fixed elementary z^2 symbol, bounded multiplication by z, coefficient weights between n^-1 and n with neighbor ratios tending to one. Such a boundary distinguishes restricted linear-fractional positive results from arbitrary weighted Hardy spaces. The exact realization matters to researchers delimiting hypotheses for future positive convergence theorems; this is not merely relabeling abstract shift nonconvergence or claiming the 2005 mechanism itself as new. It does not address classical Hardy, weighted Bergman, nor Question 5.1.
